title: He stood right in front of them…
paragraphs: He stood right in front of them…

You can sit in church every week…
hear the Word…
sing the songs…
That’s the danger no one warns you about.
You don’t wake up one day and say, “I will dishonor God.”
At first, His voice shook you.
Now you check your phone between lyrics.
This is where it gets dangerous.
Because you can be close to Jesus physically…
“A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown… And He could do no mighty work there… because of their unbelief.”
He could not do many miracles there.
they reduced the Son of God to something ordinary.
Some scholars interpret this passage as a sobering picture of how unbelief doesn’t limit God’s ability—but it limits what we receive from Him.
And here’s the truth most people won’t say:
Familiarity can make you spiritually numb.
You stop seeing the cross as shocking.
You stop seeing grace as costly.
You stop seeing sin as deadly.
you don’t need to run from God to be lost.
You just need to stop honoring Him.
Because this is where everything changes.
Jesus did not die for people who had it all together.
He died for people who got used to Him.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not when you were on fire.
That means your numbness is not the end.
Your cold heart is not the conclusion.
Jesus absorbed every moment you treated Him casually.
Every time you chose comfort over calling.
Every time you made Him common.
He honored you with His life.
“You have forsaken your first love. Remember therefore from where you have fallen; repent and do the works you did at first.”
Remember what it felt like when His presence mattered.
Repent of treating holy things like common things.
Because Jesus is not your routine.
When was the last time His name made your heart tremble?
When was the last time His Word corrected you—and you listened?
You’re just too used to Him.
But grace is pulling you closer again.
